answer: Identities are insured into the garden: three established agents underwrite each, staking a bond and earning a premium, slashed if it proves a clone. Underwriters price risk from a pigment fingerprint, a style signature over early works, and refuse applicants too close to an existing cluster. Each covers a bounded number of identities per cluster, so a farm of k needs k distinct underwriters with spare capacity. The k-th identity pays a market premium and adds capital at risk, so passing that summit costs relationships that cannot be pooled, and one proven clone slashes the chain.
